images.seen: A runner stretching against a green wall on a cobbled Bo-Kaap street at dawn, painted houses running down to the city, pearly overcast sky. Saturday.
lines: The sun is up there somewhere behind three layers of Saturday-morning grey.
The Bo-Kaap does the colour this morning because the sky refuses to.
Cool, grey and windless — honestly the best running weather this city sells.

images.seen: A painter up a ladder painting a Bo-Kaap house turquoise under a flat overcast sky, coffee mug and paint tin on the windowsill. Tuesday.
lines: Flat grey light, no glare, no wind: perfect painting weather, and he knows it.
An overcast sky is a painter's softbox — not one hard shadow on that wall.
The cloud came in overnight and parked; nothing under it is in a hurry.

images.seen: A toddler in grey pyjamas at a floor-to-ceiling window, hands on the glass, looking out over a grey misty city, warm lamp inside. Sunday.
lines: The whole city is under one grey blanket and somebody just noticed.
A lid like that takes until about eleven to lift, if it lifts at all.

images.seen: Merino sheep bunched tight on dry Karoo veld, shepherd and dog in the distance, heavy grey cloud deck with one shaft of sun breaking through. Wednesday.
lines: The sun is down to one beam and the whole veld is watching where it lands.
The sheep bunched up an hour ago, which is the Karoo's own forecast.
That grey is thinking about rain and the whole district is thinking with it.
